name: SwapX arbitrary transferFrom on approval holders
summary: SwapX's swap entry point 0x4f1f05bc takes the token owner as a caller-supplied argument and runs transferFrom on it into a caller-chosen pair without checking that the owner is the caller. Anyone could swap any SwapX approver's balance into pools they had pumped; the attacker swept 59 BUSD approvers at once and copycats drained approvers for years.
notes: Campaign and loss come from Approval logs naming SwapX as spender with an owner other than the tx sender (5,389 txs incl. the anchor, none before it; sampled traces show SwapX transferFrom from the owner). Tokens that emit no Approval on transferFrom (e.g. WBNB) are not covered, so this is a lower bound.

Loss is the owners' net token outflow per tx: stables at par, others at DefiLlama prices near the block; 69 unpriced tokens are excluded. LZ (one 9.9M LZ wallet drained by the attacker in 0xaee8ef10) is valued at that tx's realised 87,861 BUSD rate, as its pool could not absorb it.
Non-upgradeable contract with no storage read on the exploit path; the runtime is unchanged since deployment.

campaign.selection: Successful transactions after the anchor, other than those listed, carrying an Approval(owner, spender=0x6d8981847eb3cc2234179d0f0e72f6b6b2421a01) log whose owner is not the transaction sender, i.e. SwapX spent a third party's allowance (Etherscan topic query on Approval with topic2 = SwapX).
